L7: # Radiation oncology trials
L8: 
L9: WCVM researchers are seeking canine patients for two radiation oncology clinical trials.
L10: 
L11: Researchers at the Western College of Veterinary Medicine (WCVM) are seeking canine patients for two radiation oncology clinical trials. If you have patients that would be potential candidates for these studies, please share this information with your clients. For more information, contact Dr. Monique Mayer. (monique.mayer@usask.ca)
L12: ###
L13: Nasal tumours
L14: 
L15: The objective of this study is to determine if cone-beam computed tomography acquired with a linear accelerator provides comparable radiation treatment planning to a diagnostic CT scan.
L16: 
L17:   * Tumour type: Nasal tumour, any histopathological diagnosis
L18:   * Species: Dog
L19:   * Inclusion: Patient will undergo radiation therapy at the VMC
L20:   * Study pays for: radiation planning CT scan, CT contrast agent
L21:   * Contact: Dr. Monique Mayer (monique.mayer@usask.ca)
L22: ### Oral melanoma
L23: 
L24: Oral melanoma is the most common malignant oral tumour diagnosed in dogs, with a high risk of distant metastasis. The objective of the first clinical trial is to determine whether PET-CT (positron emission tomography-computed tomography) technology provides more accurate staging information than computed tomography (CT) alone for dogs with oral melanoma.
L25:   * Tumour type: Oral melanoma
L26:   * Species: Dog
L27:   * Inclusion: Gross disease, no prior radiation therapy or chemotherapy
L28:   * Study pays for: PET-CT, MRI, immobilization, $500 toward invoice
L29:   * Contact: Dr. Monique Mayer (monique.mayer@usask.ca)
L30: ### Contact information
L31: 
L32: Dr. Monique Mayer, DVM, MSc, DACVR (Radiation Oncology)
L33: monique.mayer@usask.ca

L8: # WCVM scientists seeking dogs with spreading cancer for clinical trial
L9: 
L10: Oncology researchers at the Western College of Veterinary Medicine (WCVM) are seeking dogs with spreading cancer for a clinical trial at the WCVM Veterinary Medical Centre.
L11: 
L12: May 20, 2024
L13: #### Deciphering tumour heterogeneity through necropsy, imaging and transcriptomics in naturally occurring cancers in dogs.
L14: 
L15: One out of every four dogs is diagnosed with cancer, and sadly, half of those animals will die of the disease. Cancer's ability to spread is a major challenge, making it difficult to detect and treat effectively.
L16: 
L17: This clinical trial at the WCVM will explore potential solutions by using a new approach to studying cancer spreading in canine patients.
L18: WCVM researchers will study cancer spreading in pet dogs diagnosed with cancer using two tools: positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) imaging, an advanced imaging technology, and RNA sequencing, a gene profiling method.
L19: 
L20: The WCVM is the only Canadian veterinary college equipped with PET-CT technology. The state-of-the-art equipment allows allows human and veterinary cancer researchers at the University of Saskatchewan to offer this unique opportunity to pet owners.
L21: #### What are the study's goals?
L22: 
L23: The WCVM researchers aim to find a way to improve cancer detection and treatment by:
L24: 
L25:   * exploring the role and benefits of PET-CT technology in understanding cancer spreading
L26:   * assessing how different genes contribute to cancers in various parts of the body
L27: #### What canine patients are eligible?
L28: 
L29: The WCVM research team is seeking dogs with advanced-stage cancer. Eligible dogs must be healthy enough to undergo anesthesia and a PET-CT scan.
L30: 
L31: After their pet's death, owners will be asked to return to the WCVM Veterinary Medical Centre for a post-mortem examination (necropsy).
L32: #### What costs will the WCVM research team cover?
L33: 
L34: Each dog enrolled in the clinical trial will undergo anesthesia and receive a PET-CT scan at no cost. In addition, there will be no charge for a post-mortem examination — a procedure that will allow the research team to gain a better understanding of the disease.
L35: #### How can pet owners find out more about this clinical trial?
L36: 
L37: If you own a dog that may be eligible for this trial, contact the study’s research team leader:
L38: 
L39: Dr. Arata Matsuyama, DVM, PhD, DACVIM (Medical Oncology), DAiCVIM (Medical Oncology)
L40: Assistant Professor, Dept. of Small Animal Clinical Sciences
L41: Western College of Veterinary Medicine
L42: arata.matsuyama@usask.ca
